Subject: FoundryCap - k6 dry‑run & perf criteria

Thanks again for the call today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the performance qualification and the customer‑led dry run. High level: Redwood will provide a staging test account, a working k6 scenario, and an IP allowlist template; FoundryCap will validate concurrency/throughput targets during a short dry run window and confirm any adjustments.

Key SLOs we discussed (please confirm):
- P95 end‑to‑end latency <= 350 ms for generation requests ~512 tokens (non‑streaming baseline).
- Sustained throughput target: 120 req/s for the main gen route (spikes to 180 req/s for short bursts).
- Concurrency: 200 concurrent streaming connections (SSE) with per‑connection token rate ~15 tok/s.
- Error budget: <1.5% 5xx or connection failures across the window.

Customer‑led dry run plan (proposed):
1) Preflight: short staging run (5–10 min) to validate scripts & credentials.
2) Dry run window: Tue Jun 10, 08:00–11:00 PT — three 30‑min ramps (ramp/hold/ramp down).
3) Post‑run readout within 1 business day with CSV of raw traces and p95/p99 metrics.

What Redwood will provide by EOD Friday (attachments):
- foundry_k6_scenario.js (k6 script + example VU profile)
- ip_allowlist_template.csv (sample CIDRs to allow from FoundryCap side)
- staging‑api‑key.txt (staging API key and endpoint info; keys rotated after run)

Action items / owners: 
- Soojin (me): schedule the dry run window, share invite & runbook link.
- Marissa Cole (engineering ops): create staging API key and stand up short demo run.
- Alex / FoundryCap Ops: confirm IP CIDRs to add to Redwood allowlist, confirm availability for Jun 10 window.

Questions for you: can you confirm the concurrency target (200 streaming connections) and whether your client will use long‑lived SSE or WebSocket sessions? Also confirm the ops contact who will be on‑call during the window.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15‑min preflight if you want to walk through the script.

—

Thanks Soojin — useful recap. Quick answers and a couple asks from our ops/engineering side: 

- Concurrency: we want to stress to 300 concurrent streaming connections (not 200) for the initial hold; that matches the client workload profile (many short‑lived connections but peaks when a campaign runs). Can you confirm the streaming SLO can be validated at 300?
- Error budget: happy with <1.5% but would like to see p99 as well (we care about tail behavior).
- Preflight: can we do a short smoke/staging run on Mon Jun 9 (late afternoon PT) before the dry run? Ops can triage any immediate config issues.

Looping in our ops email above. Also please put the staging endpoint and test key in a secure note rather than plain text in email (we’ll share secure SFTP for logs later).

If Jun 10 is the run window, I can make the first ramp slot.
